headline.title: First flakes for Adirondacks.
headline.text: Up to {{s:1.9}} on the summit of Whiteface Sunday night to Monday afternoon, and {{s:7.4}} for the week. 18 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in Northern Vermont and Western Maine. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
A cooler and unsettled pattern is expected this weekend with summit level snow possible Sunday morning.
Another round of precipitation expected for the start of the work week, with this activity more focused in the favored upslope areas of the northern mountains.
Remaining unsettled midweek through the end of the week, likely trending cooler by next weekend.

ALY.excerpt:
) An upper level low will bring periods of rain to the region today into early Sunday though no hydrological impacts are expected.
) Some additional light showers are expected next week as a series of disturbances pass through the area before a larger upper trough builds overhead later in the week.

GYX.excerpt:
Beneficial rainfall expands inland tonight with locally heavy rainfall along the coast with more showery conditions expected this weekend.
Cooler temperatures arrive later this weekend and remain through next week areawide. There will be multiple chances for light precipitation, including light snow or snow showers for the higher peaks of the White Mountains.

PHI.excerpt: A cold front passes through the region this morning and cooler and drier air builds into the region.

CTP.excerpt: ) Seasonably cooler this weekend into next week with bulk of precipitation confined near and southeast of Lake Erie

RLX.excerpt:
) Pleasant days and chilly nights are expected through early next week, with frost/freeze conditions possible most mornings.
) Next precipitation chances arrive with a system late next week.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Sunday night to Monday afternoon: Smugglers' Notch {{s:1.8}}, Burke {{s:1.5}}, Jay Peak {{s:1.4}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.2,4.1}} at Smugglers' Notch. Rain mixes in at the bases.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:27}} to {{t:47}}, with up to {{s:1.7}} of snow.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 40).
Trend: totals have come down since yesterday.
NWS Burlington forecasters, Saturday 6:43 AM: "A cooler and unsettled pattern is expected this weekend with summit level snow possible Sunday morning."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

writeups.name: New Hampshire
writeups.title: Some snow Saturday night, best at Bretton Woods.
paras: Light snow Saturday night to Sunday morning: Bretton Woods {{s:3.1}}, Cannon {{s:3}}, Wildcat {{s:1.2}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:1.3,8.1}} at Bretton Woods. It's a northwest upslope setup, one that usually favors Bretton Woods, Cannon and Wildcat. Rain mixes in at the bases.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:28}} to {{t:51}}, with up to {{s:3.1}} of snow and gusts near {{w:41}} up top.
Bretton Woods usually opens first here, around Nov 15. Wildcat gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 22).
Trend: totals have gone up since yesterday, led by Bretton Woods ({{s:3.4}} to {{s:5.3}}).
NWS Gray forecasters, Saturday 6:18 AM: "Beneficial rainfall expands inland tonight with locally heavy rainfall along the coast with more showery conditions expected this weekend."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

writeups.name: New York
writeups.title: Some snow early Friday, best at Hunter.
paras: The main event runs early Friday to Friday night. Hunter {{s:4.7}}, Windham {{s:4.6}}, Belleayre {{s:4.1}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0,19.8}} at Hunter. It's a nor'easter setup, one that usually favors Hunter, Windham and Belleayre. Confidence is low so far (30% odds of {{s:6}}+), so expect changes.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:1.6}} at the summit Tuesday afternoon to Tuesday night (models {{r:0.2,2.7}}). Snow level near {{e:2900}}, so the base ({{e:1800}}) mixes with or changes to rain Tuesday evening: about {{s:0}} there vs {{s:1.6}} up top. Highs stay near {{t:30}} afterward, so some of it should stick up high.

Cold enough to make snow Thursday afternoon to Friday night: about 33 hours at or below {{t:26}} at mid-mountain, counting humidity. One more cold stretch follows this week. Whether the guns run is up to the resort.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 20 days out.
